subject.title: Exploring a chat-first Android surface for OpenClaw (discussion + possible focused upstreaming)

question: Should the official Android app adopt a chat-first default or explicit mode, accept only focused UX/media PR slices while keeping the current companion-node shell, or leave chat-first Android forks external for now?
rationale: Current main partially improves Android chat access, but changing the default surface or accepting broader media/navigation fork slices affects onboarding, pairing, permissions, release posture, and Android product direction.

options.title: Scope focused Android PR slices
options.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define narrow launch/navigation, media, and connectivity slices that need real-device proof before PR acceptance.

options.title: Keep the official app Overview-first
options.body: Document that the official app remains an Overview-first Gateway companion and ask contributors to file only specific defects or small polish PRs.

options.title: Sponsor a chat-first mode
options.body: Have maintainers explicitly sponsor a chat-first default or mode and require onboarding, upgrade, media-permission, and release proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Scope focused Android PR slices
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define narrow launch/navigation, media, and connectivity slices that need real-device proof before PR acceptance.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily affects Android app launch, navigation, and chat/media surfaces, where obviyus is the listed area owner and strongest code-history owner.
